subject: Strange issue with constraints in different specifications of the same model

messages.author: 135bca318fc12657
messages.subject: Strange issue with constraints in different specifications of the same model
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I'm having an issue with constraints behaving weirdly across different ways of specifying the same model. I'm working with the STARTS model, which decomposes variance in multiple waves of a variable (X) into purely stable trait variance, variance that has an autoregressive structure, and state variance unique to each wave.

There are multiple ways to specify this model. For instance, if you predict each observed X from a latent stable trait and a latent autoregressive trait, then the residual can be considered the "state" component of the STARTS model. This should be equivalent to a model that defines an explicit "state" latent variable for each wave, but sets the residual variance of each observed X to 0.

For some extensions that I want to do, I'd prefer to use the latter approach, where I define an explicit latent state variable. However the STARTS usually has a stationarity constraint, and imposing this constraint works when I specify the model the first way, but does not work when I specify it the second way (even though the constraint doesn't refer to this state component or the residuals for the observed variables; it relates to the autoregressive part, which is the same in both).

Specifically, if I specify a model where there is no explicit state variable and the residuals for each X are estimated (model labeled "starts" below), then I get the same estimates as the alternative specification, where I include an explicit latent state variable (model labeled "starts_s" below).

If I add a stationarity constraint to the first model (shown in the model labeled "starts_c" below), the model runs and the estimates make sense. However, if I add the exact same constraint to the second specification (shown in the model labeled "starts_s_c" below), this results not just in negative variances, but in estimates that make no sense.

Any thoughts?

Hi Rich,

It looks like lavaan wanders off into huge negative variances. If you write instead:
ri_x ~~ lower(0)*ri_x

And also add below your constraint, two others:
v > 0
v2 > 0

It converges to the same solution as the equivalent model:

On Thursday, January 26, 2023 at 2:13:24 PM UTC-8 richard...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi Everyone,

I'm having an issue with constraints behaving weirdly across different ways of specifying the same model. I'm working with the STARTS model, which decomposes variance in multiple waves of a variable (X) into purely stable trait variance, variance that has an autoregressive structure, and state variance unique to each wave.

There are multiple ways to specify this model. For instance, if you predict each observed X from a latent stable trait and a latent autoregressive trait, then the residual can be considered the "state" component of the STARTS model. This should be equivalent to a model that defines an explicit "state" latent variable for each wave, but sets the residual variance of each observed X to 0.

For some extensions that I want to do, I'd prefer to use the latter approach, where I define an explicit latent state variable. However the STARTS usually has a stationarity constraint, and imposing this constraint works when I specify the model the first way, but does not work when I specify it the second way (even though the constraint doesn't refer to this state component or the residuals for the observed variables; it relates to the autoregressive part, which is the same in both).

Specifically, if I specify a model where there is no explicit state variable and the residuals for each X are estimated (model labeled "starts" below), then I get the same estimates as the alternative specification, where I include an explicit latent state variable (model labeled "starts_s" below).

If I add a stationarity constraint to the first model (shown in the model labeled "starts_c" below), the model runs and the estimates make sense. However, if I add the exact same constraint to the second specification (shown in the model labeled "starts_s_c" below), this results not just in negative variances, but in estimates that make no sense.

Any thoughts?

parts: Hi Keith, see this paper: https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2021.1982716 (and in particular, Appendix D). I think it's very new.
